titulo_es: Verbs followed by -ing or the infinitive (2)
descripcion_es: Verbs that change meaning with -ing or to (remember, forget, stop, try, regret, go on) and verb + object + infinitive.
resumen: Some verbs take both -ing and to + infinitive, with different meanings. Others require person + to + infinitive (want someone to do), and make/let take the infinitive without to.

filas: recall something done earlier: I remember locking the door.
not forget to do something: Remember to lock the door.
forget something you experienced (mostly in the negative): I'll never forget meeting her.
not remember to do something: I forgot to call him.
no longer do something: He stopped smoking.
pause in order to do something else: He stopped to smoke.
test something to see if it works: Try restarting the computer.
make an effort, attempt: I tried to open the window, but it was stuck.
be sorry about something in the past: I regret selling my car.
be sorry to announce (formal): We regret to inform you…
continue doing the same thing: She went on talking.
move on to do something else: He went on to become president.

explicacion.texto: Verb + person + to + infinitive: want, would like, expect, ask, tell, allow, encourage, persuade, force, teach. I want you to stay (not “I want that you stay”).
Make and let take person + infinitive without to: She made me apologise. They let us leave early. In the passive, make takes to again: I was made to apologise.

items: Like, love, hate, prefer, begin, start, continue take both forms with almost no change in meaning.
Need + -ing has a passive meaning: The car needs washing (= needs to be washed).
Help takes the infinitive with or without to: She helped me (to) move.

ejemplos.frase: Did you remember to buy milk?
I clearly remember visiting this museum as a child.
ejemplos.traduccion: Recuerdo perfectamente haber visitado este museo de niño.

ejemplos.frase: We stopped to look at the view.
If you can't sleep, try drinking a glass of warm milk.
ejemplos.traduccion: Si no puedes dormir, prueba a tomarte un vaso de leche caliente.

ejemplos.frase: My parents encouraged me to study abroad.
ejemplos.traduccion: Mis padres me animaron a estudiar en el extranjero.

ejemplos.frase: The teacher made us rewrite the essay.
ejemplos.traduccion: El profesor nos hizo reescribir la redacción.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I want that you come with me.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I want you to come with me.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Want + person + to + infinitive, never want that.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: She made me to wait for an hour.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: She made me wait for an hour.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Make + person + infinitive without to (in the active).

errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Don't forget to lock the door.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Not remembering to do a pending task: forget + to.

ejercicios.frase: I'll never forget ___ (see) the Northern Lights for the first time.
ejercicios.explicacion: The forget row in the table applies: forget + -ing means forgetting something you experienced, and it is used mostly in the negative (I'll never forget). The clue is “for the first time”: it refers to an experience that has already happened and remains as a memory. That is why forget seeing. With to see it would mean forgetting to do a pending task.
ejercicios.traduccion: Nunca olvidaré la primera vez que vi la aurora boreal.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Forget + to means not remembering to do a pending task; here it is a memory of something experienced.
The infinitive without to does not follow forget.
The perfect form would be having seen, but here seeing is enough and is the natural choice.

ejercicios.frase: Please remember ___ (switch) off the lights when you leave.
ejercicios.explicacion: The remember row applies: remember + to + infinitive means not forgetting to do a pending task. The clue is “when you leave”: switching off has not been done yet; it lies ahead. That is why remember to switch off. With switching it would mean recalling having switched something off before.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Not forgetting to do a pending task: remember + to.
ejercicios.traduccion: Por favor, acuérdate de apagar las luces cuando te vayas.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Remember + -ing means recalling something already done; here the action is future and pending.
A word-for-word copy of Spanish “acordarse de”: remember takes no preposition; for a pending task use to + infinitive.
To is missing: remember + to + infinitive.

ejercicios.frase: We were tired, so we stopped ___ (have) a coffee.
ejercicios.explicacion: The stop row applies: stop + to + infinitive means pausing in order to do something else. The clue is “We were tired, so…”: they stop what they were doing (travelling, walking) in order to have a coffee. That is why stopped to have. With having it would say they gave up having coffee.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Pausing to do something else: stop + to.
ejercicios.traduccion: Estábamos cansados, así que paramos a tomar un café.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Stop + -ing means no longer doing something: it would say they gave up having coffee, the opposite of what is meant.
A word-for-word copy of Spanish “parar para”; purpose is expressed with to + infinitive, not with for + -ing.
In English, for does not introduce an infinitive of purpose; say to have.

ejercicios.frase: The printer isn't working. Have you tried ___ (turn) it off and on again?
ejercicios.explicacion: The try row applies: try + -ing means testing something as a possible solution to see if it works. The clue is “The printer isn't working”: a remedy is being suggested. That is why tried turning. Try + to would mean making an effort to do something difficult, which is not the case here.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Testing something as a solution: try + -ing.
ejercicios.traduccion: La impresora no funciona. ¿Has probado a apagarla y volverla a encender?

errores_previstos.explicacion: Try + to means attempting something difficult; to suggest a solution to test, use -ing.
The infinitive without to does not follow try.

ejercicios.frase: After a short pause, the speaker went on ___ (talk) for another hour.
ejercicios.explicacion: The go on row applies: go on + -ing means continuing to do the same thing you were doing. The clue is “After a short pause… for another hour”: she returns to the same activity, talking. That is why went on talking. Go on + to would indicate moving on to a new activity.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Continuing the same activity: go on + -ing.
ejercicios.traduccion: Tras una breve pausa, el orador siguió hablando otra hora más.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Go on + to means moving on to do something different; here the same activity continues, so it is -ing.
The infinitive without to does not follow go on.

ejercicios.frase: I regret ___ him the truth; now he's angry with everyone.
ejercicios.explicacion: The regret row applies: regret + -ing means being sorry about something already done. The clue is the second part, “now he's angry”: telling the truth has already happened and had consequences. That is why regret telling. Regret + to is a formal phrase for announcing bad news (We regret to inform you).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Being sorry about something in the past: regret + -ing.
ejercicios.traduccion: Me arrepiento de haberle dicho la verdad; ahora está enfadado con todo el mundo.

por_opcion.telling: Correct: regret + -ing for being sorry about something in the past.
por_opcion.to tell: Incorrect here: regret to tell means “I am sorry to have to tell you” and announces bad news about to be given.
por_opcion.tell: Incorrect: the infinitive without to does not follow regret.

ejercicios.frase: My parents didn't let me ___ out late.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that make and let take person + infinitive without to. The clue is let me: let means “to allow” and requires the bare infinitive. That is why let me stay. Allow has the same meaning but does take to (allowed me to stay).
ejercicios.traduccion: Mis padres no me dejaban quedarme fuera hasta tarde.

por_opcion.stay: Correct: let + person + infinitive without to.
por_opcion.to stay: Incorrect: to is not used with let; it would be correct with allow (didn't allow me to stay).
por_opcion.staying: Incorrect: let is not used with -ing.

ejercicios.frase: The manager expects everyone ___ on time.
ejercicios.explicacion: Expect is in the list of verbs with person + to + infinitive. The clue is expects everyone: after the person, the verb takes to. Where Spanish uses “que” + subjunctive (“espera que lleguen”), English uses object + to + infinitive: expects everyone to arrive.
ejercicios.traduccion: El director espera que todos lleguen puntuales.

por_opcion.arrive: Incorrect: to is missing; only make and let are used without to.
por_opcion.arriving: Incorrect: expect does not take -ing after the person.
por_opcion.that arrive: Incorrect: a word-for-word copy of Spanish “que”; also, the sentence makes no sense without a subject after that. With that you would need expects that everyone arrives/will arrive, a different structure.

ejercicios.frase: She trained as a nurse and went on ___ a hospital director.
ejercicios.explicacion: The go on row applies: go on + to + infinitive means moving on to do something new, to a next stage. The clue is the sequence “trained as a nurse and went on…”: after training, her career moves on to another position. That is why went on to become. With becoming it would say she continued becoming, which makes no sense.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Moving on to a new stage: go on + to.
ejercicios.traduccion: Se formó como enfermera y llegó a ser directora de un hospital.

por_opcion.to become: Correct: go on + to for a new step in a sequence (she eventually became).
por_opcion.becoming: Incorrect: go on + -ing means continuing with what you were doing, not moving on to another stage.
por_opcion.become: Incorrect: the infinitive without to does not follow go on.

ejercicios.frase: I'd like that you meet my parents.
respuestas: I'd like you to meet my parents.
I would like you to meet my parents.
ejercicios.explicacion: The structure on the card applies: would like + person + to + infinitive. The mistake in the sentence is a word-for-word copy of Spanish “me gustaría que + subjunctive”, with that. In English the person becomes the object (you) and the verb takes to: I'd like you to meet. The uncontracted form, I would like, is also accepted.
ejercicios.traduccion: Me gustaría que conocieras a mis padres.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I'd like that you meet my parents.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: would like is not followed by that + clause.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I'd like you meet my parents.
errores_previstos.explicacion: To is missing: would like + person + to + infinitive.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I'd like you to meeting my parents.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After to comes the infinitive, meet.

ejercicios.frase: The film made me to cry.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card states that make, in the active, takes person + infinitive without to. The clue is made me: the subject causes someone to do something. That is why made me cry, without to. Only in the passive does it take to again (I was made to cry).

errores_previstos.respuesta: The film made me to cry.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: make in the active does not take to.
Make is not used with -ing; it takes the infinitive without to.
After make + person comes the infinitive, not the past tense.

ejercicios.frase: He has stopped to drink coffee because it keeps him awake.
respuestas: He has stopped drinking coffee because it keeps him awake.
ejercicios.explicacion: The stop row applies: stop + -ing means no longer doing something. The clue is the reason, “because it keeps him awake”: he has given up the habit. With to drink the sentence would say he has paused in order to have a coffee, which contradicts the reason given. The correction is stopped drinking.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ha dejado de tomar café porque le quita el sueño.

errores_previstos.respuesta: He has stopped to drink coffee because it keeps him awake.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: stop + to means pausing in order to have coffee.

errores_previstos.respuesta: He has stopped drink coffee because it keeps him awake.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After stop you need -ing, not the infinitive without to.

errores_previstos.respuesta: He has stopped of drinking coffee because it keeps him awake.
errores_previstos.explicacion: A word-for-word copy of Spanish “dejar de”; stop is followed directly by -ing.

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite the sentence in the passive, starting with We.
ejercicios.frase: The guards made us wait outside.
respuestas: We were made to wait outside.
We were made to wait outside by the guards.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card points out that in the passive make takes to again: be made to + infinitive. The clue is the instruction, which asks you to start with We and change to the passive. The object us becomes the subject We, the verb made becomes were made and the next verb takes to: We were made to wait outside. The agent by the guards is optional.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: In the passive, make takes to again.

errores_previstos.explicacion: In the passive, make requires to: were made to wait.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We were made to waiting outside.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After to comes the infinitive, wait.
The auxiliary were is missing; without it, it is not passive and the sentence makes no sense.

respuestas: she persuaded me to join the gym
ejercicios.explicacion: Persuade is in the list of verbs with person + to + infinitive. The order is subject (she), verb (persuaded), person (me), to + infinitive (to join) and object (the gym). Spanish says “me convenció para que me apuntara”, with a subordinate clause; in English the infinitive with to is enough.
ejercicios.traduccion: Me convenció para que me apuntara al gimnasio.

errores_previstos.respuesta: she me persuaded to join the gym
errores_previstos.explicacion: The object pronoun me goes after the verb, not before it as in Spanish.

errores_previstos.respuesta: she persuaded to join me the gym
errores_previstos.explicacion: The person goes immediately after persuade: persuaded me to join.

ejercicios.explicacion: The remember row applies: remember + -ing means recalling something already done. The clue is the words given, with posting in -ing: posting the letter happened before remembering it. The order is subject, remember, -ing verb and its object: I remember posting the letter.
ejercicios.traduccion: Recuerdo haber echado la carta al correo.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Remember is the main verb and goes right after the subject; posting comes after it.
The object the letter goes after posting (post the letter).

descripcion_larga_es: Some English verbs take both -ing and to + infinitive, but with different meanings: remember, forget, stop, try, regret and go on. Others require person + to + infinitive (I want you to stay), and make and let take the infinitive without to. It is B2 level because a mistake changes the message (giving up smoking versus stopping to smoke) and because Spanish uses “que” + subjunctive where English does not.

contexto.que_es: They are three advanced verb + verb patterns. First, verbs whose meaning changes depending on whether they take -ing or to (remember, forget, stop, try, regret, go on). Second, verbs that take person + to + infinitive (want, would like, expect, ask, tell, allow, persuade). Third, make and let, with person + infinitive without to, except make in the passive.
contexto.por_que_importa: Choosing the wrong form doesn't just sound bad; it changes the meaning: “He stopped to smoke” says he paused to smoke, not that he gave it up. The structure want someone to do replaces the Spanish subordinate clause with “que”, and the word-for-word copy “I want that you…” is one of the most recognisable mistakes made by Spanish speakers. These contrasts are often tested in B2 exams.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When you talk about memories and tasks (remember, forget), changes of habit (stop), solutions you test (try), regrets (regret) or what you want or make others do (want, make, let). The signal is time: -ing usually looks back at something earlier or in progress; to looks ahead to something later or pending. Where Spanish says “quiero que vengas”, English uses want you to come.
